what: Full scored authorization path under load (k6), compared with rules-only on the same workload
hardware: Apple M3 Pro, 18 GiB memory, macOS 15.3.1; Docker Desktop 29.5.3 with 11.67 GiB memory
k6: v2.3.0 (official macos-arm64 release, checksum verified), run natively against 127.0.0.1:8086
stack: make up (Compose profiles stream + packaged): PostgreSQL 16, Redis 7.4, Kafka 3.9.1, Kotlin API (Java 17), outbox publisher, Python ONNX scorer (one uvicorn process), feature and case consumers, case API, console
workload: bench/load_full.js: constant arrival rate for 15 s; one fresh card per authorization (15 x rate cards, setup excluded from timing); each card on its own device and usual merchant category; amounts SGD 1.20-800; merchant risk drawn from 0.05-0.9 (3 of 7 levels at 0.35 or above); about 3% abroad; 4% small-amount bursts on one card from a new device
measurement: auth_duration is the client-side time of POST /v1/authorizations. Fallback is modelAction RULES_FALLBACK (scorer missed the API's 50 ms limit or failed). Queue drain is the time after k6 ended until this run's outbox rows were all published and the feature and case consumer groups had zero lag, polled about every 3-7 s, so it is coarse. Cases opened is the growth of the case store, which opens a case when the model score is at least 0.1.
cold_definition: API and scorer containers restarted immediately before the run; Kafka, Redis, PostgreSQL and consumers kept running
not_comparable_to: The 11 October k6 runs (bench/k6_100_summary.json, k6_500_summary.json) used bench/load.js (one merchant, fixed amount, 50-100 cards), an older k6, and paused Kafka, Redis and outbox publisher. They stay as separate history.
workload_design_notes: Two earlier designs were discarded before these measurements: 100 cards with a small shared device pool, and 5 x rate cards. With repeat purchases seconds apart on a card, the synthetic model declined 85-98% of traffic, so those runs measured an unrealistic pattern. Their raw files were not kept as evidence.
limits: One machine, local loopback, synthetic traffic and a synthetic model; not a production capacity claim.
Decline share is a property of this workload and model, not a fraud rate.
Single run per setting; no repeated trials or confidence intervals.
